units.text: INT. MONASTERY WINE CELLAR - EVENING
Barrel vaults of ancient brick, sweating with damp.
Rows of oaken casks stretch away into shadow like sleeping animals.
One candle, stuck on a keg, throws a trembling gold circle onto the flagstones.
A wounded soldier in a torn gray greatcoat sits slumped against a cask with his boots off and a filthy bandage around his thigh.
He is a STRANGER to this place, forty, unshaven, eyes sharp even in pain.
His rifle lies across his lap, its muzzle pointed at the stairs.
On the stairs, a pair of old sandals descends.
BROTHER AMBROSE, 70s, white-haired, in a brown habit patched at the knee, carries a bowl of broth and a loaf of black bread.
He stops three steps from the bottom.
I have brought supper.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: The Stranger does not answer.
The rifle does not move.
You may shoot me after you eat. It would be a waste to shoot me before.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: Put it on the floor.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Ambrose sets down the bowl and bread on the bottom step.
He retreats.
The Stranger drags himself forward, takes the bowl, drinks, hands shaking.
He tears the bread with his teeth.
There is a doctor in the village. He is not one of yours, but he is a good doctor.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: My own doctors are dead.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: All of the doctors are dead, my son. The ones left are only men.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: The Stranger studies him.
His shoulders sag a fraction.
He sets the bowl down.
Lukas. My name is Lukas.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Lukas. I am Ambrose.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: The monks, are there others?
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Eleven. Upstairs. Praying for rain.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: It will rain.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: It always does. Then the walls weep.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: Footsteps overhead.
Boots, many pairs, ringing on flagstone.
A voice barks a command in another tongue.
Dust sifts from the ceiling into the candle.
Lukas lifts the rifle.
Ambrose raises both palms.
They are not yours.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: They are not yours either.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Lukas turns to the cask beside him and puts a hand on the bung.
Ambrose watches, grave.
The boots stop above the cellar door.
A latch clanks.
Lukas, in the name of God, put it down.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: Ambrose, in the name of God, hide.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Ambrose does not move.
Captain! The cellar door is unbarred!
units.name: SERGEANT VOGEL

units.text: The door cracks open at the top of the stairs.
A thin white line of lamplight falls down the steps.
CAPTAIN ISOLDE KESSLER, 30s, black coat, officer's cap, steps through.
A pistol in her gloved hand, held low.
She descends, slowly, boots ringing, into the candlelight.
Good evening, Brother. Good evening, soldier.
units.name: KESSLER

units.text: Good evening, Captain.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: You are bleeding on the church's floor.
units.name: KESSLER

units.text: Forgive me.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: She stops on the bottom step.
Looks at the bowl, the bread, the rifle.
A very long silence.
Brother Ambrose, I came to count the casks. I find only eleven.
units.name: KESSLER

units.text: There were twelve, Captain.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: And the twelfth?
units.name: KESSLER

units.text: The twelfth is a man.
units.name: BROTHER AMBROSE

units.text: Kessler lowers the pistol an inch.
Lukas does not lower the rifle.
The candle gutters.
Overhead, thunder rolls.
Soldier, it is raining.
units.name: KESSLER

units.text: It always does.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: She turns her head to the stairs and listens.
Beyond the door, her men shuffle.
There is no one here. Resume the search upstairs.
units.name: KESSLER

units.text: The boots retreat.
The latch closes.
Kessler holsters the pistol.
She sits on the step, takes off her cap, and runs her hand through her hair.
Eat. All of you.
units.name: KESSLER
